questions.q: Make it negative: « Il fume encore. » → Il ne fume ___ .
questions.why: Ne … plus is the negative of encore: not any more. Ne … jamais is the negative of toujours.

questions.q: Make it negative: « Je vois quelqu'un. » → Je ne vois ___ .
questions.why: Personne is the negative counterpart of quelqu'un, as rien is of quelque chose: je ne sais rien.

questions.q: Make it negative: « J'ai un livre. » → Je n'ai pas ___ livre.
questions.why: After a negative, un / une / du / de la / des all collapse to de. It elides before a vowel: je n'ai pas d'idée.

questions.q: Which negation of « C'est un problème » is correct?
questions.why: The article survives after être. The other survivor is the definite article: je n'aime pas le café, never pas de café there.

questions.q: Build the sentence: I haven't eaten.
questions.why: In a compound tense the light words pas, plus, jamais and rien sit between the auxiliary and the participle.

questions.q: Build the sentence: I saw nobody.
questions.why: The heavier words personne, aucun, que, ni … ni and nulle part come after the participle, because they attach to what follows: je n'ai vu personne, but je n'ai rien vu.

questions.q: Where does the negation go with an infinitive: « I'd rather not go » ?
choices: Je préfère ne pas y aller.
Je ne préfère pas y aller.
Je préfère ne y aller pas.
questions.why: Before an infinitive both halves stay together in front: ne pas y aller, ne rien dire, ne jamais oublier. Ne pas splits only around a conjugated verb.
Personne and rien can be the subject, and ne still appears before the verb: Personne ne sait, Rien n'est facile.

questions.q: Why is « Il ne mange que des légumes » not « que de légumes » ?
choices: Because ne … que is a restriction, not a negation, so the article survives
questions.why: Ne … que means only. The sentence stays positive, so des is untouched. Compare the real negative: il ne mange pas de légumes.

questions.q: What is the difference between « Je ne bois que du thé le matin » and « Je ne bois du thé que le matin » ?
choices: The first restricts the drink, the second restricts the time
The first restricts the time, the second restricts the drink
questions.why: Que goes immediately before the thing being restricted, so moving it moves the meaning: tea and nothing else, versus the morning and no other time.

questions.q: Answer: « Tu ne viens pas ? » — ___, je viens !
questions.why: Si is the yes that contradicts a negative question. Answering oui there is wrong; English has to fall back on stress instead.

questions.q: « Je n'aime pas le café. » — you don't either. What do you say?
questions.why: Aussi agrees with a positive, non plus with a negative. Moi si would mean you do like it, and moi non would answer a positive statement.

questions.q: Type what you hear, in correct written French.
questions.why: Rien is a light word, so it lands before the participle. In speech you would hear j'ai rien vu, with ne dropped, but the written form keeps it.

questions.q: Which negative words go before the past participle and which go after? Give the two lists and one example each.
a: Before the participle: pas, plus, jamais, rien — Je n'ai pas mangé, Je n'ai rien vu. After the participle: personne, aucun, que, ni … ni, nulle part — Je n'ai vu personne, Il n'est allé nulle part.
questions.why: The short light words hug the auxiliary; the heavier ones that behave like nouns or determiners follow the participle, because they attach to what comes next.

questions.q: Say this out loud, in full written form: I don't know.
questions.why: In conversation this collapses to j'sais pas, with ne gone entirely. Understand the dropped form, but produce the full one in writing and in any formal register.
